questions.prompt: A contributor opens a PR with 1,800 lines mixing a bug fix, a refactor, and reformatting. What should the reviewer suggest?

options.text: Splitting the PR into smaller, focused PRs (reformat/refactor separate from the bug fix) so each can be reviewed safely

questions.prompt: In `git bisect`, after marking a known bad commit and an older good commit, what does Git do?

options.text: Checks out the midpoint commit so you can test and narrow down the exact regressing commit in O(log N) steps

code.source:
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good v1.4.0

questions.prompt: Match each PR review comment style to its effect.

rows.label: Actionable & specific ('Consider extracting X so Y is testable')
Labeled non-blocking nit (`nit: typo in comment`)
Vague dismissal ('This is bad, rewrite it')

columns.label: Guides the author clearly toward a concrete improvement
Separates minor polish from merge-blocking issues
Creates friction without explaining what needs to change

questions.prompt: Why is **stale-bot auto-closing** every issue after 14 days often harmful?

options.text: It frustrates users reporting real, reproducible bugs that simply haven't been triaged yet

questions.prompt: Which practices make **GitHub Actions / CI workflows** secure in public repos? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Pinning third-party actions to full commit SHAs rather than mutable `@main` tags
Avoiding `pull_request_target` with untrusted PR code checkout

questions.prompt: When bumping from `v1.4.2` to `v2.0.0` in SemVer, what must accompany the release?

options.text: A migration guide and changelog entry listing every breaking change and upgrade step

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a **Dependabot / Renovate** PR?

options.text: Automatically opening PRs to update dependencies and patch known CVEs, verified by CI

questions.prompt: Why should **test fixtures** in a repo avoid large binary blobs when small text/synthetic fixtures work?

options.text: Large binaries bloat Git history permanently for every future clone

questions.prompt: What does `git commit --amend` do on an unpushed local commit?

options.text: Updates the most recent commit with staged changes or a new message

questions.prompt: Which items should be verified in a **release checklist**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Annotated tag and checksums/signatures are published
Skipping tests to release 5 minutes earlier
CI is green on the exact release commit

questions.prompt: When a PR fixes a bug, why should the author include a **regression test** that fails without the fix?

options.text: Because Git requires 10 files per PR
To prove the fix works and prevent the exact same bug from returning in future refactors

questions.prompt: What is **cherry-picking** (`git cherry-pick <sha>`) used for in release branches?

options.text: Copying a single bugfix commit from `main` onto a `release/1.x` branch without merging unrelated features

code.source:
git checkout release/1.x
git cherry-pick -x a1b2c3d

questions.prompt: Match each documentation type (Diátaxis) to its user goal.

columns.label: Learning-oriented step-by-step lesson for a newcomer
Goal-oriented recipe to solve a specific real-world problem
Accurate, structured API/CLI specification for quick lookup

questions.prompt: What is **reproducible build** / **provenance attestation** (e.g., SLSA)?

options.text: Verifiable cryptographic proof linking a published binary/package back to its exact source commit and CI build

questions.prompt: Why should **API breaking changes** in a library first go through a deprecation cycle when possible?

options.text: It removes the need for SemVer
Abruptly removing symbols forces downstream users to pin old versions and miss security patches

questions.prompt: Which signals suggest a dependency is **risky** to adopt in a project? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Active maintenance with clear SemVer releases
No commits, releases, or issue responses for years with open security bugs

questions.prompt: What does `git log --oneline -n 10` display?

options.text: The last 10 commits in a compact one-line-per-commit format

questions.prompt: In **code review**, what is the value of **draft PRs**?

options.text: They signal early work-in-progress to gather architectural feedback before polishing everything

questions.prompt: Why should **generated build artifacts** (e.g., `dist/`, `node_modules/`, compiled binaries) usually be in `.gitignore`?

options.text: They clutter diffs, cause merge conflicts, and are deterministically rebuilt from source by CI

questions.prompt: What is a **CODEOWNERS** file used for?

options.text: Automatically requesting review from designated maintainers when specific paths are modified

questions.prompt: Which practices help **onboard new contributors** effectively? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Requiring contributors to guess undocumented build flags
Documenting exact local setup and test commands in `CONTRIBUTING.md`
Maintaining curated `good first issue` tickets with pointers to relevant files
Providing a fast local test command that works without proprietary cloud credentials

questions.prompt: What is **trunk-based development**?

options.text: Keeping 20 long-lived branches unmerged for a year
Short-lived feature branches merged frequently into a single always-releasable `main` branch

questions.prompt: When a **flaky test** fails intermittently in CI, what is the right engineering response?

options.text: Quarantine or fix the root cause (race condition, shared state, wall-clock dependency) so CI stays trustworthy
Re-run CI 5 times and ignore it

questions.prompt: What does **dual-licensing** (e.g., `MIT OR Apache-2.0` in Rust) provide?

options.text: Users may choose either license, maximizing compatibility across ecosystems
Users must obey both conflicting licenses at once

questions.prompt: Match each release channel to its audience.

columns.label: Early adopters testing bleeding-edge features; APIs may change
Feature-frozen build for final regression testing before GA
Production teams needing stability and security backports over years

questions.prompt: Why is **signing commits or release artifacts** (GPG / Sigstore) valuable?

options.text: It cryptographically verifies author/publisher identity and artifact integrity

questions.prompt: What should a maintainer do when **archiving** an unmaintained project?

options.text: Transfer ownership to a random unknown account
Add a clear notice in `README.md`, point to maintained alternatives/forks if any, and mark the repository archived/read-only

questions.prompt: What is a **conventional commit** prefix like `feat:` or `fix:`?

options.text: A structured commit-header convention enabling automated changelog generation and SemVer bumps

questions.prompt: What does `git push --force-with-lease` do compared to `git push --force`?

options.text: It refuses to overwrite the remote branch if someone else pushed new commits you haven't fetched yet

questions.prompt: Which practices improve **issue tracker hygiene**? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Deduplicating repeat reports onto one canonical issue
Linking fixing PRs with `Fixes #123` so issues close cleanly on merge

questions.prompt: Why should **feature flags** or **experimental opt-ins** guard unfinished features merged to `main`?

options.text: They allow incremental integration into `main` without exposing half-built behavior to default users

questions.prompt: What is a **monorepo** vs. **polyrepo** trade-off?

options.text: Monorepos simplify atomic cross-package changes and shared CI, while polyrepos isolate permissions and release cycles

questions.prompt: Why is **CI caching** (e.g., caching dependency downloads) important for contributor experience?

options.text: Fast CI feedback (<5 min) keeps contributors engaged and cuts wasted compute

questions.prompt: What does `git blame <file>` help you discover?

options.text: Which commit and author last modified each line, linking back to the PR/issue explaining *why*

questions.prompt: What is **fuzz testing** in open-source security-critical libraries?

options.text: Feeding millions of mutated/random inputs to uncover crashes, panics, or memory bugs

questions.prompt: Why should **release notes** highlight **contributors** and **upgrade risks**?

options.text: It helps operators assess upgrade safety and recognizes community effort

questions.prompt: Which governance practices help larger open-source projects scale? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Using RFCs / design proposals for major architectural changes
Having more than one maintainer with release/admin access (raising bus factor)
Keeping all architectural decisions in private DMs
Documenting how contributors earn triage or committer status

questions.prompt: What is **typosquatting** in open-source package registries?

options.text: Publishing malicious packages with names nearly identical to popular libraries to trick installers

questions.prompt: When should you **reject** (politely close) a feature PR in an open-source repo?

options.text: When it falls outside the project's core scope or adds maintenance burden you cannot support long-term

questions.prompt: What is **CVE** coordination when patching a vulnerability?

options.text: Publishing a CVE identifier and security advisory alongside the patched release so users know to upgrade

questions.prompt: What is **automated release tooling** (e.g., release-please / GoReleaser) good for?

options.text: Generating consistent artifacts, checksums, changelogs, and tags from CI without manual laptop steps

questions.prompt: What is the ultimate measure of a **successful open-source project**?

options.text: Reliable software that solves real problems, backed by clear docs, tests, governance, and a sustainable community
